text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
SOYBEAN SALE - South Korea bought 50,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans from Japanese trading house Marubeni Corp for May 1-20 shipment.
- South Korea bought 20,000 tonnes U.S. No. 1 soybeans at $321.12 a tonne, FOB, from Continental Grain for April 25-May 15 shipment.
BARLEY SALE - Cyprus on Friday bought 25,000 tonnes of barley from Tradigrain SA Geneve for $150.82 per ton C & F for May shipment.
WHEAT SALE - Argentina sold 17,000 tonnes of wheat to Brazil for $185 a tonne, not including freight, for May shipment.
SOYOIL TENDER - Taiwan on Friday passed on a tender for 2,500 tonnes of soyoil.

OILSEED TENDER - South Korea will tender Tuesday for 53,500 tonnes of oilseeds, including 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal, 6,500 tonnes cottonseed meal, 8,000 tonnes of grain screening pellet and 25,000 tonnes of palm kernel meal.
WHEAT TENDER - Jordan will tender for 120,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter and/or northern spring wheat on May 1 for May/June shipment.
- Taiwan will retender on April 23 for two shipments of U.S. wheat totalling 68,000 tonnes. Taiwan had passed on the tender on Tuesday due to high prices.
WHEAT TENDER - Iraq will tender on April 18 for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for June arrival.
- CCC seeks up to 7,220 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat, maximum moisture 13.5 percent, under the export program for Bosnia for May 7-31 shipment.
DURUM TENDER - Algeria seeks 100,000 tonnes of optional durum wheat for shipment in May and June.
SORGHUM TENDER - The CCC will tender April 22 for up to 5,000 tonnes sorghum for export to Kenya, May 5-31 shipment.
BARLEY TENDER - Turkey's tender for 150,000 tonnes of barley contains three shipments of 50,000 tonnes of white feed and malting white barley for May 15-22, June 1-15 and June 1-15 shipment.
RICE TENDERS - Costa Rica will tender April 16 for 26,500 tonnes optional origin long grain rough rice or 18,000 tonnes long grain milled rice.
- South Korea is expected to tender at the end of June to buy 77,000 tonnes of rice to meet its 1997 WTO quota.

MARKET TALK - A vessel that left Brazil on March 31 with a cargo of 53,362 tonnes of soybeans bound for the United States arrived at the mouth of the Mississippi River on Friday morning...Brazil stevedore union officials said representatives from Cosipa would hold talks Friday to try to resolve a labor dispute...The Thai government has not yet decided when 200,000 tonnes of corn can be imported under the zero-tariff program as local price conditions have not been met...Thai authorities also said they would soon discuss the possible elimination of the current 10 percent soymeal import tariff.
